questions.q: What is the difference between a trailing and a centered rolling window?
options: Trailing uses only today and the past; centered also uses future values
why: Correct. That is why centered windows leak in forecasting.
Centered includes today and values on both sides.

questions.q: s = [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]. What is s.rolling(3).mean() at the last row?
questions.why: The last window is [12, 16, 20]. The mean is 16.

questions.q: EWMA, alpha = 0.3. S(t−1) = 100 and y(t) = 200. What is S(t)?
A span of 19 in pandas ewm means which alpha? (alpha = 2 / (span + 1))
You want features for predicting the sales of day t. Which feature is leak-free?
options: s.rolling(7).mean() when s[t] is the target
why: Correct. The window ends at day t−1.
Centered windows include days after t.
That window includes the target value itself.

questions.q: A sensor value jumps to a new level and stays there. Which smoother follows the jump fastest without looking ahead?
options: Trailing mean with a large window
EWMA with a very small alpha
why: Correct. A large alpha gives high weight to the newest value.
A large window averages many old values, so it reacts slowly.
A small alpha reacts very slowly.

questions.q: You are plotting the trend of the last two years for a report. Which window is fine?
options: A centered window, because you are describing the past
why: Correct. Centered windows have no delay. They are fine when nothing is predicted.
Trailing windows are needed for forecasting inputs, not for descriptions.
Smoothing is a normal way to describe a trend.
